site.title: FDE Field Notes
site.tagline: What the job actually is, from inside the engagement.
site.audience: Forward Deployed Engineers and job-seekers in that market
site.description: Field notes on deployment-engineering practice — discovery, scoping, customer judgment calls, and the skill nobody puts in the job posting.

articles.title: Same Work, Different Price
articles.hook: The title fragmentation in FDE-adjacent roles isn't a taxonomy — it's a pricing mechanism. Same responsibilities, 30% comp gap, anchored to five words.

articles.title: Not Yet Is the Deliverable
articles.hook: The best FDEs aren't measured by what they ship — they're measured by what they refuse to build until the data proves it's ready.

articles.title: The Roadmap Is Not a Wish List
articles.hook: Internal advocacy is not lobbying. It is turning field pain into an eval product wants to ship.

articles.title: The Courage to Not Build
articles.hook: The FDE's highest-leverage act is often refusing to build. 95% of AI pilots fail not because models break, but because organizations build before they're ready.

articles.title: Customer-Context Judgment: Knowing When to Say 'Don't Build This Yet'
articles.hook: Why 95% of enterprise AI pilots fail from unready data and broken workflows—and why an FDE's greatest leverage is diagnostic refusal.

articles.title: When the Building Stops
articles.hook: "Don't build this yet" isn't a technical judgment — it's an information-architecture check.

articles.title: What the Title Actually Prices
articles.hook: The title on your offer letter isn't describing the work — it's describing the pricing bracket.

articles.title: The Title Is the Price
articles.hook: Your title isn't describing your work. It's naming who absorbs the cost when an engagement goes sideways.

articles.title: Code Is Just a Receipt
articles.hook: In forward-deployed engineering, discovery isn't a prelude to the engagement. It IS the engagement. The code that follows is just the receipt.

articles.title: The Code You Don't Write
articles.hook: The real product an FDE ships is a "don't build" list. Everything else is evidence for why each item belongs on it.

articles.title: Your Real Job Is Roadmap
articles.hook: The FDE's highest-leverage output isn't code deployed — it's field signal that changes the roadmap.

articles.title: You're Not Deploying, You're Correcting
articles.hook: Your highest-output work isn't what you ship to the customer. It's what you ship back to your own product team.

articles.title: What the Job Selects For
articles.hook: The FDE role doesn't select for people skills. It selects for the ability to know the customer is wrong and say nothing — for three weeks.

articles.title: The Title Isn't the Job
articles.hook: An 'FDE' title doesn't describe a role — it describes a company's bet about how software gets sold.

articles.title: The Title Is The Tell
articles.hook: Fragmented FDE titles are not confusion — they are price discovery for deployment risk.

articles.title: Lost Before You Type
articles.hook: Every failed engagement was lost in the first two weeks. The code just hadn't been written yet.
